analysis.title: GS Armbrust - What Matters Today: TMT Earning Beats are not Being Rewarded, HF Performance and Positioning in October, The Fed as a Driver of Long Term Rates, Apple Disappoints, Previewing the Midterm Elections, Sector Sentiment Trends (3 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth is tracking +33% y/y with 60% of companies reported. That matches Q2 but ends the acceleration seen in Q1 and Q2. Median stock EPS growth slowed to 12% from 14%.
GIR expects about 30% EPS growth in 2026 excluding non-recurring items, slowing to 18% in 2027. Consensus 2027 EPS is up only 2% since the season started.
The median stock beating EPS estimates outperformed the S&P 500 by 152bp the day after reporting, above the historical median. TMT beats have generally gone unrewarded.

60% of companies beat by more than one standard deviation, above the 50% historical average but below the 64% average of the past four quarters. Analysts have cut margin estimates as energy prices rise.

Hyperscaler capex is on track for about $800bn in 2026 (+96%) and is expected to reach $1.2tn in 2027 (+44%), with little revision this season. AI infrastructure EPS growth is expected to peak at 80% this quarter and slow to about 40% by late 2027.

Hyperscalers reported combined negative free cash flow of -$31bn in Q3. Cloud revenue for AMZN, GOOGL and MSFT grew 54% y/y and is still accelerating, but crowded positioning set a high bar and results raised concern about AI disrupting other businesses' revenues.

Breadth is widening. Since the season began 70% of S&P 500 stocks are up but they are only 50% of index market cap, so the index is down 3% while the S&P 500 ex-AI is up 5%. Energy prices and interest rates are the key determinants of whether non-tech can keep rising.

Hedge funds had a rough October: Fundamental L/S -3.5% and Systematic L/S -3.6%, the first time since 2016 that both cohorts fell 3% or more. Global equities saw the largest dollar net selling since March, and net leverage fell at the fastest pace since March.

HFs rotated out of TMT and Cyclicals into Defensives. Info Tech saw the largest dollar net selling since June, and Defensives were net bought for the first time in 7 months, led by Staples and Health Care.

GS argues the latest break higher in forward rates came with the Fed's shift to a new hiking cycle. It sees the Fed-driven and the structural explanations (deficits plus AI investment financing needs) as compatible, since policy reflects an economy with those structural forces. The market updates its view of neutral rates mainly through shifts in actual Fed policy ranges.

AAPL fell 4% pre-market on EPS. December-quarter gross margin was guided to 45%-46%, about 140bps lower sequentially, with memory costs the main cause. Services growth of about 10% in Q4 is guided to slow to 8%-9% in December versus ~12% consensus. China sales missed estimates by nearly $1B.
PLTR fell 8% after guiding a slowdown in bookings growth. AMD and Arista report today, giving reads on accelerator demand and hyperscaler networking spend after Intel and the optical sell-off.

GS expects Democrats to win the House with a wider margin, and the Senate looks closer. Fiscal deadlines are the main legislative focus, with the next on Dec. 11 when spending authority expires. Reversing spending cuts would add about 0.25% of GDP to 2027 spending.

GS expects Trump to announce new tariff increases after the election that more than offset tariff reductions, raising the US effective tariff rate by a little under 2pp. A national data center tax incentive moratorium is unlikely, and AI regulation compromise is possible but restrictive regulation is unlikely.

AAPL reported EPS this week and guided December-quarter gross margin to 45%-46%, with Services growth guided to 8%-9% versus ~12% consensus expectation.
AAPL China sales fell nearly $1B short of estimates.
PLTR guided a slowdown in bookings growth and fell 8%.
AMD and Arista are scheduled to report today (3 Nov 2026).
Cloud revenue for AMZN, GOOGL and MSFT grew 54% y/y combined in the reported quarter.

risk_factors: Energy prices rising, leading analysts to cut margin estimates.
Crowded positioning in hyperscalers sets a high bar for results.
AI disruption of other businesses' revenues.
Memory cost inflation pressuring gross margins (AAPL).
Fed hiking cycle pushing forward rates higher.
Post-election tariff increases and fiscal deadline brinkmanship.
vol_and_positioning: Fundamental L/S returned -3.5% and Systematic L/S -3.6% in October, the first time on record (since 2016) both fell 3% or more.
Global equities saw the largest dollar net selling since March, driven by equal amounts of short and long sales.
Overall net leverage fell at the fastest pace since March while gross leverage rose, driven by mark-to-market. Fundamental L/S net leverage declined, led by Asia L/S funds.
Every region except DM Asia was net sold, led by EM Asia and North America.
HFs rotated out of TMT and Cyclicals into Defensives. Info Tech saw the largest dollar net selling since June, and Defensives were net bought for the first time in 7 months.
geopolitical: The war in Iran is expected to be a top Democratic agenda item around fiscal deadlines.
Tariff rollback is on the Democratic agenda, but GS expects Trump to announce new tariff increases after the election.
Midterm elections next week: prediction markets imply high odds of a Democratic House majority, with the Senate closer.
Dec. 11 is the next deadline when spending authority expires, and the debt limit will also need to be raised.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud revenue for AMZN, GOOGL and MSFT grew 54% y/y and is still accelerating, with hyperscaler capex expected to reach $1.2tn in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Beats in TMT go unrewarded because crowded positioning set a high bar. AI capex growth looks to be peaking, hyperscaler free cash flow was -$31bn, and AI infrastructure EPS growth is expected to slow from 80% to about 40% by late 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The reaction to guidance from AMD and Arista reporting today may matter as much as the guidance itself, and a rewarded TMT beat would challenge the bear read.

tension_points.theme: Fed versus structural drivers of long rates
tension_points.bull_case: Structural forces (persistent fiscal support and AI investment demand) justify a persistently higher rate structure.
tension_points.bear_case: The latest break higher in forward rates came with the Fed's shift to a new hiking cycle, not structural drivers or major macro events.

tension_points.bull_case: 70% of S&P 500 stocks are up since the season began and the S&P 500 ex-AI is up 5%.
tension_points.bear_case: The index is down 3% because AI leaders fall back, and higher energy prices and interest rates could stall the non-tech advance.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A worsening outlook for energy prices and interest rates would end the non-tech rally.
